A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same sparse preference-learning work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments in Figures 1-2 and reward-modeling experiments in Figure 3 and Appendix B, including Tables 3-4.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds frozen-backbone reward-modeling results in Figure 4 and learned-sparsity measurements in Section 4.2.

M1.justification: The linear reward model, ℓ0-constrained estimator, and ℓ1-regularized objective remain unchanged. The added frozen-backbone experiments instantiate the existing fixed-feature formulation rather than introducing a new estimator or loss.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic preference data and reward modeling on rm-static and SHP; SHP already appears in v1 Appendix B. Frozen-backbone training changes the experimental configuration, not the datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: Synthetic experiments retain maximum likelihood as the comparator, and real-data experiments retain the corresponding unregularized model with β = 0. The new frozen-backbone study uses this same comparator; no additional comparison method is evaluated.

E3.justification: v3 adds a distinct real-data evaluation protocol that freezes Llama-3.2-1B and trains only its reward head, sweeping n from 200 to 6400 with β = 0.5 × n^-0.5. This substantially expands evaluation of sample efficiency under fixed features. Existing synthetic and full-fine-tuning settings, including batch sizes, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 4 extends sample-size sensitivity analysis to frozen Llama features on both real datasets. Section 4.2 also examines how sparse the learned parameters are at n = 800 and 3200. Earlier synthetic sparsity and sample-size analyses and regularization sweeps are retained.

E5.justification: The retained experiments keep their 20 synthetic repetitions and five or three real-data trials, with unchanged disclosed seeds. Figure 4 extends the existing five-trial reporting practice; repeated-run plots and shaded bands already appear in v1. No new confidence-level or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: v3 adds learning curves showing higher frozen-backbone accuracy with ℓ1 regularization across the evaluated sample sizes on both datasets. It also reports sparsity ratios of 4.5% and 7.5% for rm-static and 4.2% and 7.2% for SHP at n = 800 and 3200. These substantially extend results under an added training regime; Figures 1-3 and Tables 3-4 retain their earlier results.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, Assumptions 3.1-3.3, Theorems 3.1-3.4, and their bounds are unchanged. The proofs move from v1 Appendix D to v3 Appendix E with equivalent mathematics; added proof pointers and formatting changes do not alter the reasoning.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the same sparse minimax rate, optimality of the ℓ0 estimator, near-optimal ℓ1 estimation under additional assumptions, and empirical benefits for reward modeling. The added experiments support these retained claims without redefining the central contributions.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the newly measured sparsity as selection of a small, informative feature subset. It also explains the resource advantages and practical uses of frozen-backbone training. Existing theoretical qualifications and future-work directions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit link to the authors' SparsePreferenceLearning repository, whereas v1 only identifies the DeepSpeed-Chat foundation. It explicitly identifies the retained real-data experiments as full fine-tuning and documents the new frozen-backbone feature dimension and regularization schedule.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds brief coverage and citations for context-dependent choice and ranking, including Bower and Balzano, Seshadri and colleagues, and Tomlinson and Benson, plus Reeves and Gastpar on sparse recovery. The overall research positioning and priority claim remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. v3 expands the sparsity motivation, distinguishes full fine-tuning from frozen-backbone experiments, corrects the Section 3.2.2 heading from ℓ0 to ℓ1, and reorganizes the appendices with an introductory roadmap.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column manuscript to a two-column conference layout, with pervasive changes to typography, spacing, and placement. Existing figures are resized and regrouped, Figure 4 adds two learning-curve panels, and appendix tables and proofs are extensively reflowed.

improvement.justification: The frozen-backbone study strengthens the connection between the fixed-feature theory and real-data sample efficiency, while measured sparsity supports the feature-selection interpretation. The repository link and clearer experimental labeling improve transparency. These are focused gains; the central theoretical contribution and earlier experimental findings remain unchanged.
